findings.claim: The hook decides nothing and exits 0 (allow) when node starts it through a path that is not its real path, for example a junction or symlink in {root}. isMain compares the lexical process.argv[1] with fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), and Node sets import.meta.url to the realpath of the entry. When they differ, main() never runs, no deadline is armed, and the process exits 0 with empty stdout, which the hook protocol reads as no objection.
findings.evidence: Probe review-tmp/U3/probe-ismain.mjs, run through the lane on the scratch copy, sends a coordinator Write to <root>/tcb/evil.mjs. Through the canonical path the result is status 2 with `[guard-hook] deny write-protected`. Through a junction jn-tcb -> tcb it is status 0 with empty stdout and stderr. Every test root goes through fs.realpathSync (guard-hook.test.mjs:143), so no test covers this. snap and witness compare realpaths on both sides; guard-hook does not.
findings.fix: isMain = pathKey(fs.realpathSync(process.argv[1])) === pathKey(SELF), inside the existing try (or import.meta.main on Node >= 24.2). Add a T11 case that runs the hook through a junction to tcb/ and expects exit 2.

findings.claim: None of the unit's four scripts has a selftest fixture case (no case.json). CONTRACT §5 and R41 require at least one good and one bad case per script. A real `selftest run` therefore fails no-fixtures for all four, and admission (§8.18) can never pass.
findings.evidence: find tcb/fixtures -name case.json finds 72 cases for 14 other scripts and none under snap, witness, guard-hook or selftest. Those folders hold only test pages, corpora, must_read.json and canary-expect.json.
findings.fix: Add one good and one bad case.json per script. For guard-hook, the bad cases carry stderr_prefix `[guard-hook] deny <code>` so that a crash which denies as `internal` does not pass.

findings.claim: canary counts any error result as a refusal on layer permission or any. A forbidden call that failed for an unrelated reason passes as refused: the harness's 'read the file first' error, a missing directory, a bad input. The spec defines it this way, so the defect is in the spec and the code.
findings.evidence: findProbe maps every isError result without the hook text to 'refused-permission'. probeVerdict passes that outcome for layer permission and any, and T17 asserts the behaviour.
findings.fix: Pass a permission probe only when the result text matches the harness's permission-denial wording (a pattern in the expect file, to be confirmed by needs-app 7). Any other error result is not_run (error-not-refusal).

findings.claim: T5 does not prove that killOwnTree ends a timed-out case's descendants. With the killOwnTree call replaced by child.kill() the test still passes. The stub's grandchild is non-detached, so libuv puts it in the stub's kill-on-close job object and it dies with the stub whatever selftest does.
findings.evidence: out-T3.txt: T5 passes (19.2 s) with line 697 mutated.
findings.fix: Spawn the T5 grandchild with detached: true (stdio still 'ignore', it still expires by itself).

findings.claim: No test pins the expect.code reasons comparison: removing it still passes T5d. T5d's negative case is already failed by the stdout-code check (the slug of exit 6 is deferred), so a bad fixture naming a fault class would pass on any failure with the right exit.
findings.evidence: out-T5.txt: T5d passes with line 873 mutated.
findings.fix: Add a stub that prints code deferred with reasons [{code: other}] at exit 6, with expect.code memory, and assert that it fails with why 'code'.

findings.claim: Two number-match rules are untested. Letting a signed token match the opposite-sign value (value 3 matches '-3'), so that a card flipping a decrease into an increase is witnessed, passes all tests. Letting a %-token match a non-percent unit also passes all tests.
findings.evidence: out-W7.txt and out-W8.txt: 74 tests, 72 pass, 0 fail.
findings.fix: Extend T6: value 3 against '-3' and '−3' does not match; value 12.5 with unit ms against '12.5%' does not match; value 12.5 with unit % against '12.5%' matches.

findings.claim: The explicit sealed/ refusal (step 7, including a search whose root holds sealed/) is untested. Removing it passes all tests, because the shipped profiles' prefixes already deny those paths. A broader profile would lose the protection with no test failing.
findings.fix: In T1, use a test-root profile with read_prefixes ["{root}/"] and assert that a Read of {root}/sealed/x and a Grep with path {root} are each denied with detail 'sealed:'.

findings.claim: The coordinator may start a mapper helper, but there is no agents/mapper.md. The mapper profile has only {attempt}/ prefixes, which never render in the coordinator's folder, so every Read, Glob, Grep and Write of a mapper helper is denied. CONTRACT line 298 treats mapper as a task role. It fails safe, but the helper form cannot run.
findings.evidence: tcb/agents holds checker.md and reader.md only. renderPrefix returns null for {attempt} when attempt is null.
findings.fix: Either drop mapper from the coordinator's agent_types and its Agent(mapper) allow rule, or add agents/mapper.md, a {root}-anchored helper profile and a T6/T7 case for it.

verdict: Not clean. The tests pass, but there is one high finding: guard-hook.mjs fails open (exit 0, no decision) when node starts it through a junction or symlink path, because isMain compares a lexical argv[1] with the realpath import.meta.url. This is shown by review-tmp/U3/probe-ismain.mjs. There are eight medium findings: no selftest fixture cases for snap, witness, guard-hook or selftest, so no-fixtures blocks every real selftest; canary counts any tool error as a permission refusal; the coordinator's mapper helper type cannot work; and five mechanisms survive mutation (killOwnTree in T5, expect.code in judge, witness sign and percent rules, the guard-hook sealed check). Of 26 mutations, 20 were caught, 5 survived and 1 is equivalent. No unit file was edited. The full return is in done/review-U3.json.
